rule.body: Use the present simple for habits and facts, and the present continuous for actions happening now. Use the past simple for finished actions at a stated past time (yesterday, ago, in 2020). Use the present perfect (has/have + past participle) for actions linked to now, often with 'since', 'for', 'already' and 'yet'. Use the past perfect (had + past participle) for an action completed before another past action.
rule.example: I have lived in Ibadan since 2019, but I moved to my present house two years ago.

questions.explanation: This is a general fact, so we use the present simple. 'Water' is singular, so the verb is 'boils'.

questions.stem: Look. The children ___ in the rain.
questions.explanation: 'Look' shows the action is happening right now, so we use the present continuous: 'are playing'.

questions.stem: We ___ the match on television yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time, so we use the past simple 'watched', not the present perfect.
'Since 2021' links the past to now, so we need the present perfect: 'has taught'.

questions.stem: My father bought this car five years ___.
questions.explanation: 'Ago' counts back from now to a finished past time and goes with the past simple 'bought'.

questions.stem: I have not finished my assignment ___.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' is used at the end of negative sentences in the present perfect. 'Already' is not used this way in negatives.

questions.stem: When I got to the bus stop, the bus ___.
questions.explanation: The bus left before I got there, so the earlier past action takes the past perfect: 'had left'.

questions.stem: While Musa ___ his homework, the light went off.
questions.explanation: An action in progress in the past that is interrupted by another takes the past continuous: 'was doing'.

questions.stem: I ___ him since we left secondary school.
questions.explanation: 'Since' marks a period from the past up to now, so the main verb takes the present perfect: 'have not seen'.

questions.stem: Kemi ___ for two hours when her friend finally arrived.
questions.explanation: The waiting went on for two hours before another past event, so we use the past perfect continuous: 'had been waiting'.
